newsitem.title: USA: U.S. energy prices up in ACCESS, towards new highs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. energy prices up in ACCESS, towards new highs.

text.p: U.S. crude oil and products prices edged up early in ACCESS trade, but volumes were moderate as traders waited for further Iraq news.
Any significant headlines could push heating oil and crude prices through key technical barriers overnight, and poise them to break life-of-contract highs on Friday, traders said.
"The number to keep an eye on is $27.70 (a barrel)," said one trader, referring to the yearly high in crude oil futures, seen back in March.
Another trader said if ACCESS prices for crude move past the intraday high of $25.30 a barrel, the March record could be broken.
Crude oil for October delivery traded at $25.07, up seven cents a barrel from the settle with 315 lots traded.
October heating oil traded at 69.50 cents a gallon, up from a settle of 69.17 cents on 45 lots.
And front-month unleaded gasoline traded at 66.05 cents a gallon, up 0.14 cents.
